answer: A sponsor carries 66% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the voyage liability is published in the whisper ledger at admission, the jetty audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must hence place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
